findings.highlight: That's exactly what I mean when I say you two are inseparable!
findings.evidenceJa: それがらぶらぶでなくてなんだっつ～の。こりゃ、マジで秒読みかな
findings.explanation: Takahiro not only insists the bento proves they are lovey-dovey but jokes that the marriage countdown may truly have begun. The translation omits 秒読み and therefore his innocent belief that the wedding is imminent.
findings.japanese:
「それがらぶらぶでなくてなんだっつ～の。
こりゃ、マジで秒読みかな」
findings.todokanai: "That's exactly what I mean when I say you two are inseparable!"

findings.highlight: You'll only cause me more worry
findings.evidenceJa: あなたは食べたら駄目。…余計な心配することになるから
findings.explanation: Setsuna's mother forbids Takahiro from eating the leftovers because he would end up worrying unnecessarily after discovering something wrong. The translation says his eating will cause the mother more worry, reversing the experiencer and obscuring that she is shielding him from knowledge.
findings.japanese:
「いいから。
あなたは食べたら駄目。
…余計な心配することになるから」
findings.todokanai: "Listen to me, don't eat that… You'll only cause me more worry…"

findings.evidenceJa: 昨夜の俺が少しでもかずさを満たしたのなら
findings.explanation: Haruki hopes that what he did the previous night satisfied or fulfilled Kazusa even a little, a charged emotional and bodily formulation. 'Made things easier' reduces that intimacy to relief from difficulty.
findings.japanese:
もし、昨夜の俺が少しでもかずさを満たしたのなら、
それに勝る喜びはない。
findings.todokanai: If I managed to make things easier for Kazusa yesterday, then there is no greater happiness for me.

findings.evidenceJa: わ、わたしは、そんなつもりなかったんだけど
findings.explanation: In Setsuna's rehearsed excuse, she denies that she personally intended to bring Haruki food or show affection; her mother supposedly made her. The translation says she disagreed with the mother's assessment that he was not eating properly, changing the protective lie she is constructing.
findings.japanese:
「春希くん、最近忙しそうだったから。
きちんとした食事してないだろうからって。
わ、わたしは、そんなつもりなかったんだけど…」
findings.todokanai: "She said that you probably haven't been eating properly, with how busy you are all the time. I didn't think so though…"

findings.highlight: half the clothes I have are work clothes
findings.evidenceJa: 持ってる服は、大半が仕事用のスーツやワイシャツ
findings.explanation: The great majority of Haruki's clothes are work suits and dress shirts. The translation reduces that dominant professional uniform to only half his wardrobe.
findings.japanese:
最低限の家具と家電。
持ってる服は、大半が仕事用のスーツやワイシャツ。
findings.todokanai: The bare minimum for any home. And half the clothes I have are work clothes and dress shirts.

findings.evidenceJa: 俺以外の、『二人目の住人』が持ち込んだもの
findings.explanation: The quoted 'second resident' is Haruki's domestic recognition of the person who frequently used the room and brought cookware, not a legal tenant or confirmed cohabitant. The translation turns the metaphor into actual tenancy.
findings.japanese: ………俺以外の、『二人目の住人』が持ち込んだもの。
findings.todokanai: …Items that the other tenant staying here had brought into the room.

findings.highlight: The current contract runs out at the end of next month. You'll have to pay that month's rent too before the end of this month.
findings.evidenceJa: 今の契約期限が３末までですから、来月末には引き払っていただくことになりますが
findings.explanation: The lease expires at the end of March, so Haruki will need to vacate by the end of next month. The translation changes the expiration date and invents a rent-payment deadline that does not appear in the source.
findings.japanese:
「今の契約期限が３末までですから、
来月末には引き払っていただくことになりますが」
findings.todokanai: "The current contract runs out at the end of next month. You'll have to pay that month's rent too before the end of this month."

findings.highlight: the history I've shared with that apartment
findings.evidenceJa: あの部屋の、味わいのある光景
findings.explanation: Alongside five years of memories, Haruki separately mourns the room's characterful view or scene—the visible mixture of their possessions. The translation repeats an abstract shared history and loses the physical domestic arrangement that will vanish in days.
findings.japanese:
五年かかって築き上げた思い出も、
あの部屋の、味わいのある光景も…
findings.todokanai: Both the memories that I've built up for the past five years as well as the history I've shared with that apartment I've lived in…
